points: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah. His mother was a harlot, but he himself was a mighty man of valour.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Gilead's wife's sons grew up and thrust out Jephthah: thou shalt not inherit in our father's house, for thou art the son of a strange woman. Strange woman here does not mean his mother was of another nation; the scripture says only that she was a harlot. His brothers cast him out of his father's house over his mother, though he had as much right to that house as they did.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers
